title: Permeable Driveways: The Hidden Flood Protection Chicago Homes Need
intro: Chicago's distinct climate and geology present a formidable opponent to conventional landscaping. Our city is built on layers of clay, which, while supportive, are notoriously poor at absorbing water. Coupled with a relatively flat topography in many areas and an aging stormwater infrastructure, every major rain event or rapid snowmelt pushes our drainage systems to their limits. When rain hits an impervious surface like a traditional concrete or asphalt driveway, it has nowhere to go but sideways, becoming runoff. This runoff picks up pollutants, overwhelms storm drains, and often finds its way into basements, leading to costly damage and persistent frustration for homeowners.
